subject: physics
name: Physics

pillars.name: Concepts
pillars.scope: The student holds a wrong idea about forces, motion, energy, waves, fields or circuits.

pillars.name: Strategy & Setup
pillars.scope: The ideas are sound, but the plan is wrong: the wrong equation or law, a wrong free-body diagram, sign convention, system or angle reference.

pillars.name: Procedure
pillars.scope: The plan is right, but carrying out the method goes wrong (rearranging, vector addition, circuit reduction, graph analysis, ray diagrams).

pillars.name: Calculation & Recall
pillars.scope: Method and plan are sound; a number, sign, constant, formula detail, unit or rounding slips.

pillars.name: Communication
pillars.scope: The physics may be right, but the answer is not what was asked, lacks a direction or unit, or is not explained.

pillars.name: Test Habits
pillars.scope: How the student handles the test: blanks, traps, giving up, not checking, not using the formula sheet.

decision_order: Is the student's idea of the physics wrong (CON)?
Is the idea right but the equation, free-body diagram, sign convention or system wrong (STR)?
Is the plan right but a step of the method done wrongly (PRC)?
Is it a slip in a number, sign, constant, formula detail, unit or rounding (FAC)?
Is the physics right but the answer not what was asked, missing a direction or unit, or unexplained (COM)?
Or is it how the test was handled (TST)?

codes.name: Motion Needs a Force
codes.plain_name: Thinks moving things need a force to keep going
codes.student_help: A net force changes motion; an object at constant velocity has zero net force.
codes.description: Believes a moving object needs a net force in its direction of motion, or that the net force points the way the object moves.
codes.example: 'The puck slides at constant speed on ice because the force of the push is still acting on it.'

tell_apart.how: If the confusion is between velocity and acceleration in kinematics (no forces involved), use CON_VELOCITY_VS_ACCELERATION.
If the student adds a 'force of motion' arrow to a diagram but otherwise reasons correctly, use STR_FREE_BODY_DIAGRAM.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: frictionless-cart thought experiment.

codes.name: Velocity vs Acceleration
codes.student_help: Acceleration is how fast velocity changes; an object can be stopped and still accelerating.
codes.description: Treats velocity and acceleration as the same thing (zero velocity means zero acceleration; a fast object has a large acceleration), or reads a v-t graph as a position graph.
codes.example: 'At the top of its flight the ball has zero acceleration because it has stopped.'

tell_apart.how: If the reasoning is about forces causing motion, use CON_FORCE_IMPLIES_MOTION.
If the student understands the quantities but takes the slope or area of a graph wrongly, use PRC_GRAPH_ANALYSIS.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: motion-sensor graph matching.

codes.name: Vectors Treated as Scalars
codes.student_help: Vectors have direction; perpendicular ones combine with Pythagoras, not addition.
codes.description: Adds, subtracts or compares vector quantities as if they had no direction (3 m east + 4 m north = 7 m; distance used for displacement).
codes.example: 'She walks 3 km east and 4 km north, so her displacement is 7 km.'

tell_apart.how: If the student knows vectors need components but combines them wrongly, use PRC_VECTOR_ADDITION.
If the magnitude is right and only the direction is left off the answer, use COM_DIRECTION_MISSING.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: tip-to-tail drawing on grid paper.

codes.name: Third-Law Pairs Misunderstood
codes.student_help: Newton's third-law forces act on two different objects, so they never cancel each other.
codes.description: Places both forces of a third-law pair on the same object, thinks they cancel, or thinks the bigger or faster object exerts the bigger force.
codes.example: 'The truck hits the car with more force than the car hits the truck.'

tell_apart.how: If the error is only in which forces are drawn on one object, use STR_FREE_BODY_DIAGRAM.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: pair-labelling exercise (force of A on B / B on A).

codes.name: Current Used Up
codes.plain_name: Thinks current gets used up in a circuit
codes.student_help: Current is the same all the way around a series loop; energy, not charge, is transferred.
codes.description: Believes current is consumed by components, so less current returns to the battery, or that the first bulb in series is brighter.
codes.example: 'The second bulb is dimmer because the first bulb used up some of the current.'

tell_apart.how: If the idea of current is right and the resistor combination is calculated wrongly, use PRC_CIRCUIT_REDUCTION.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: ammeter readings at several points in a series loop.

codes.name: Energy Not Conserved
codes.plain_name: Lost track of where the energy goes
codes.student_help: Energy is never used up; it is transferred or transformed, often to thermal energy.
codes.description: Has energy appear or disappear, confuses energy with force or power, or treats 'energy lost' to friction as vanishing rather than becoming thermal energy.
codes.example: 'At the bottom of the ramp the cart has no energy left, so it stops.'

tell_apart.how: If the idea is right but the wrong energy equation is chosen, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: energy bar charts (before, transfer, after).

codes.name: Outward Force in Circular Motion
codes.plain_name: Added an outward force in circular motion
codes.student_help: In circular motion the net force points to the centre; the 'outward pull' is inertia, not a force.
codes.description: Draws or uses an outward centrifugal force, or thinks an object released from circular motion flies straight outward.
codes.example: 'When the string breaks, the ball flies directly away from the centre.'

tell_apart.how: Use this code when the outward force comes from a wrong idea; use STR_FREE_BODY_DIAGRAM for other missing or extra forces.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: release-point demonstration with tangent lines.

codes.name: Wave Properties Misunderstood
codes.plain_name: Mixed up what changes when a wave changes medium
codes.student_help: Frequency is set by the source; when a wave enters a new medium its speed and wavelength change.
codes.description: Believes waves carry matter along, that frequency changes when a wave enters a new medium, or that louder sounds travel faster.
codes.example: 'Light slows down in glass, so its frequency decreases.'

tell_apart.how: If the idea is right but the wrong wave equation is picked, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: rope-junction demonstration.

codes.name: Formula / Law Misselection
codes.student_help: The formula or rule used here does not fit this type of question.
codes.description: Applies a formula, theorem or law whose conditions the problem does not meet.
codes.example: Given v₁, a and Δt, and asked for Δd, uses v₂² = v₁² + 2aΔd, which has two unknowns, instead of Δd = v₁Δt + ½aΔt².

tell_apart.how: Here the formula itself is wrong for the situation; in STR_WRONG_SUBSTITUTION the formula is right but the givens go into the wrong places.
Here a different, real formula is chosen; in FAC_FORMULA_RECALL the right formula is chosen but remembered wrongly.

codes.remediation: Condition check table: list each formula with the conditions it needs, then tick which ones the question meets.

codes.name: Free-Body Diagram Error
codes.plain_name: Free-body diagram has missing or extra forces
codes.student_help: Draw only forces that something touching the object (or gravity) exerts on it.
codes.description: Leaves a force out of the free-body diagram (normal force, friction, tension) or adds one that doesn't exist (a 'force of motion', the applied force after release).
codes.example: Block on an incline: draws gravity and friction but no normal force.

tell_apart.how: If an extra force comes from believing motion needs a force, use CON_FORCE_IMPLIES_MOTION.
If all forces are present but resolved along the wrong axes, use STR_ANGLE_REFERENCE.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: force-agent checklist (what exerts it, on what).

codes.name: No Consistent Sign Convention
codes.plain_name: Mixed up which direction is positive
codes.student_help: Pick which way is positive at the start and give every vector its sign from that choice.
codes.description: Does not choose a positive direction, or switches it partway, so values like g, displacement or velocity carry inconsistent signs.
codes.example: Takes up as positive for the initial velocity (+12 m/s) but uses g = +9.8 m/s² for a ball thrown upward.

tell_apart.how: If the signs are set up consistently and a sign slips in the arithmetic, use FAC_SIGNED_NUMBER.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: sign-convention box at the top of every solution.

codes.name: Wrong Angle Reference
codes.plain_name: Used sin where cos was needed (or the reverse)
codes.student_help: Sketch the right triangle and check which side is opposite your angle.
codes.description: Resolves a vector using the wrong trig ratio because the angle is measured from a different line than assumed (from the vertical, from the incline).
codes.example: On a 30° incline writes the component of gravity along the slope as mg cos 30°.

tell_apart.how: If a force is missing entirely, use STR_FREE_BODY_DIAGRAM.
If the ratio is right but the calculator is in radians, use FAC_CALCULATOR_ENTRY.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: labelled component triangle drawn for every vector.

codes.name: Wrong System Chosen
codes.plain_name: Chose the wrong object or system
codes.student_help: Decide which object (or group of objects) you are applying the law to, and include only forces or momenta for that system.
codes.description: Applies a law to the wrong system: uses the total mass for one object, conserves momentum across a system with a large external force, mixes forces on different objects in one Fnet.
codes.example: Two blocks pulled together: finds the tension between them using Fnet on the whole system.

tell_apart.how: STR_FREE_BODY_DIAGRAM is about forces on one chosen object; this code is about choosing the object or system itself.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: system-boundary sketch before writing Fnet = ma.

codes.name: Wrong Substitution
codes.plain_name: Values put in the wrong places
codes.student_help: The right formula was used, but values went into the wrong spots.
codes.description: Puts known values into the wrong variables of a correct formula.
codes.example: Puts the final velocity in for v₁ in v₂ = v₁ + aΔt.

tell_apart.how: If the formula is wrong for the situation, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION; this code is only for the right formula filled in wrongly.
If the student read the number itself wrongly from the question, use TST_MISREAD_GIVEN; here the number is read right but given the wrong role.

codes.remediation: Givens list: symbol, value, unit for every quantity before any substitution.

codes.name: No Viable Plan
codes.student_help: The first move here could not lead to the answer. Plan the method before writing.
codes.description: Starts with a move that cannot reach the answer, or moves symbols around with no method.
codes.example: Projectile problem: writes three kinematics equations mixing horizontal and vertical values with no plan for which direction gives the time.

tell_apart.how: STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION is one wrong choice inside a sensible plan; this code is for when no workable plan is visible at all.
If there is only an answer with no work, use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS; this code needs visible work that wanders.

codes.remediation: Plan-first prompt: name the target, the known quantities and the bridge between them before calculating.

codes.name: Experimental Design Flaw
codes.student_help: Change one thing, measure one thing, and keep everything else the same.
codes.description: Gets the independent, dependent or controlled variables wrong, leaves out a control or repeats, or designs a test that cannot answer the question.
codes.example: Measures the period of a pendulum to study length but changes the release angle each trial.

tell_apart.how: This code is about how the experiment is set up; COM_OBSERVATION_VS_INFERENCE is about how the results are reported.
STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN is for calculation problems; use this code for planning an investigation.

codes.remediation: Fair-test frame: I will change ___, measure ___, and keep ___ the same; repeat ___ times.

codes.name: Step Omission
codes.student_help: A needed step in the method was skipped.
codes.description: Skips a required step of the procedure, so the result does not follow.
codes.example: Projectile: finds time in the air from the vertical motion, then skips multiplying by the horizontal velocity and reports the time as the range.

tell_apart.how: Here a middle step is missing and the answer is wrong; in PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION the work is right but stops before the end.
If the plan itself is missing, use STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN; here the plan is right and one step drops out.

codes.remediation: Faded worked example: complete the one missing step in an otherwise finished solution.

codes.name: Rearranging Error
codes.student_help: Rearrange with symbols first, then put the numbers in.
codes.description: Rearranges an equation incorrectly to isolate the unknown (divides instead of multiplies, moves a term without changing its sign, loses a square).
codes.example: Rearranges Ek = ½mv² for v as v = 2Ek/m (forgets the square root).

tell_apart.how: If the algebra is right and only a number is computed wrongly, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.
If the starting formula is wrong, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION; this code is for a right formula rearranged wrongly.

codes.remediation: Symbol-first rearranging drill with a check by substituting simple numbers.

codes.name: Vector Addition Error
codes.student_help: Add x-components together and y-components together, then use Pythagoras and tan⁻¹ for the result.
codes.description: Knows vectors need components but adds them wrongly: mixes x and y, gives components the wrong sign for their quadrant, or takes tan⁻¹ of the wrong ratio.
codes.example: Adds the x-component of one vector to the y-component of the other.

tell_apart.how: If the student adds magnitudes directly, use CON_VECTOR_AS_SCALAR.
If each component is computed with the wrong trig ratio, use STR_ANGLE_REFERENCE.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: component table (vector, x, y, sign).

codes.name: Circuit Reduction Error
codes.student_help: Series resistors add; parallel resistors add as reciprocals, and you flip at the end.
codes.description: Combines resistors wrongly: adds parallel resistors directly, forgets to take the reciprocal at the end, or treats a mixed circuit as all series.
codes.example: Two 6 Ω resistors in parallel: writes 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3, so R = 1/3 Ω.

tell_apart.how: If the student's idea of current is wrong, use CON_CURRENT_USED_UP.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: redraw-and-reduce one step at a time.

codes.name: Graph Analysis Error
codes.plain_name: Read the slope or area wrongly
codes.student_help: On a d-t graph slope is velocity; on a v-t graph slope is acceleration and the area is displacement.
codes.description: Takes the slope where the area is needed (or the reverse), reads a single point instead of a slope, or uses the wrong rise or run.
codes.example: Finds displacement from a v-t graph as the final velocity times the time, ignoring that the graph is a sloped line.

tell_apart.how: If the student misunderstands what the quantities mean, use CON_VELOCITY_VS_ACCELERATION.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: slope-or-area decision chart.

codes.name: Ray Diagram Error
codes.plain_name: Drew the ray diagram with the wrong rules
codes.student_help: Use two standard rays: parallel then through F, and through the centre (or through F then parallel).
codes.description: Applies the ray rules wrongly (parallel ray not sent through the focal point, rays not extended for virtual images), so the image position or type is wrong.
codes.example: Converging lens: draws the parallel ray refracting straight through without bending toward F.

tell_apart.how: If the diagram is right but the image, F or axes are unlabelled, use COM_MISSING_LABELS.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: three-ray template.

codes.name: Stage Handoff Error
codes.student_help: The final values from one stage become the starting values for the next.
codes.description: In multi-stage problems (motion that changes acceleration, collision then slide), does not carry the end values of one stage into the next, or restarts from the original givens.
codes.example: Car speeds up then brakes: uses v₁ = 0 for the braking stage instead of the speed reached in stage 1.

tell_apart.how: If the student never splits the problem into stages, use STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: stage table with a 'carry over' column.

codes.name: Stopped Before the End
codes.student_help: Read the question again when you think you are done: is your last line the thing it asked for?
codes.description: Correct work that stops before the requested quantity or form is reached.
codes.example: Asked for the speed at impact, finds the vertical component only and stops.

tell_apart.how: If the student aimed at a different target from the start, use COM_ANSWERED_DIFFERENT_QUESTION; here they were heading to the right target and stopped.
If an intermediate value is boxed as if it were final, use TST_DISTRACTOR_TRAP; if the work simply ends, use this code.

codes.remediation: Completion checklist: target quantity, unit, form asked for.

codes.name: Arithmetic Slip
codes.student_help: The steps make sense, with a small calculation slip in the numbers.
codes.description: An isolated arithmetic error with a sound method.
codes.example: Computes 9.8 × 2.5 as 2.45.

tell_apart.how: If the formula was rearranged wrongly before any arithmetic, use PRC_REARRANGEMENT.
If the slip comes from how the number was keyed in (brackets, exponent, mode), use FAC_CALCULATOR_ENTRY.

codes.remediation: Five-item rapid micro-drill on the same operation.

codes.name: Signed Number Slip
codes.student_help: A slip happened when adding, subtracting or multiplying negative numbers.
codes.description: Arithmetic slip with negatives in otherwise correct work.

tell_apart.how: Use this code when the slip is about the sign; other arithmetic slips are FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Integer operations micro-drill.

codes.name: Copy Error
codes.student_help: A number or sign changed when copying from one line to the next.
codes.description: Miscopies a digit, sign or term from one of the student's own lines to the next.
codes.example: Writes 12.5 m/s on one line and 15.2 m/s on the next.

tell_apart.how: If the value was read wrongly from the question itself, use TST_MISREAD_GIVEN; this code is for copying between the student's own lines.
If a value was calculated wrongly rather than copied, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Line-to-line check habit.

codes.name: Formula Recall
codes.student_help: The right formula was chosen but remembered with a piece missing or changed.
codes.description: Picks the right formula but recalls it wrongly.
codes.example: Writes kinetic energy as Ek = mv².

tell_apart.how: If a different formula was chosen, use STR_FORMULA_MISSELECTION.
If the formula was on the provided sheet, use TST_REFERENCE_SHEET_UNUSED.

codes.remediation: Formula flash cards with units for each symbol.

codes.name: Unit Conversion
codes.student_help: A unit conversion was off, like centimetres to metres.
codes.description: Converts units wrongly or mixes units in one calculation.
codes.example: Uses 90 km/h directly in an equation with metres and seconds.

tell_apart.how: Here the number is wrong because of a conversion; in COM_MISSING_UNITS the number is right but the unit is not written.
If the conversion factor is right and the multiplication goes wrong, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Dimensional conversion bridge: write the factor as a fraction that cancels the old unit.

codes.name: Rounding / Precision
codes.student_help: A number was rounded too early or to the wrong decimal place.
codes.description: Rounds too early, or breaks the precision the question asks for.
codes.example: Rounds the time to 1 s halfway through and gets a final distance off by 20%.

tell_apart.how: If the digits themselves are wrong, not just how many are kept, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Precision rules card: count significant figures in the givens, keep guard digits, round once.

codes.name: Calculator Entry
codes.student_help: The calculator was set up or used wrong, like being in radians instead of degrees.
codes.description: Wrong calculator mode, missing brackets when keying, or misread display.
codes.example: Calculator in radian mode: sin 30 = −0.988.

tell_apart.how: Use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP for mental or written arithmetic; this code is for results that only make sense as a keying slip (for example an answer off by a power of ten).

codes.remediation: Calculator entry drill with the same expression typed three ways.

codes.name: Constant Recall Slip
codes.plain_name: Used the wrong value for a constant
codes.student_help: Check constants (g, c, k) against the data sheet.
codes.description: Uses a wrong value for a physical constant (g = 10 or 98 m/s², c = 3 × 10⁶ m/s, wrong exponent on k or G).
codes.example: Uses the speed of light as 3.0 × 10⁶ m/s.

tell_apart.how: If the constant was printed on the provided data sheet, use TST_REFERENCE_SHEET_UNUSED.
If the formula, not the constant, is misremembered, use FAC_FORMULA_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: constants flash cards.

codes.name: Answered a Different Question
codes.student_help: The work solved for something slightly different from what the question asked.
codes.description: Gives a correct answer to a different target than the one asked.
codes.example: Asked for the maximum height, gives the time to reach it.

tell_apart.how: If the work was heading to the right target and stopped short, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION.
If a whole labelled part (b) is missing, use TST_SKIPPED_PART.

codes.remediation: Prompt deconstruction box: circle the verb, underline the target.

codes.name: Missing Units
codes.student_help: The final answer is missing its units.
codes.description: Omits units on a measurement answer.
codes.example: Gives the force as '24.5' with no newtons.

tell_apart.how: If the number is wrong because of a conversion, use FAC_UNIT_CONVERSION.

codes.remediation: Unit slot habit: draw a box after the answer for the unit.

codes.name: Direction Missing
codes.plain_name: Left the direction off a vector answer
codes.student_help: Velocity, displacement, force and momentum answers need a direction, like [E 30° N] or 'down the ramp'.
codes.description: Gives a correct magnitude for a vector quantity but no direction, or a direction that does not use the convention set up in the question.
codes.example: Final answer: 'v = 25 m/s' when the question asks for the velocity.

tell_apart.how: If the student combined vectors as scalars, use CON_VECTOR_AS_SCALAR.
If the unit is missing, use COM_MISSING_UNITS.

codes.remediation: Tier 4: final-answer template with magnitude, unit and direction slots.

codes.name: Unsupported Answer
codes.student_help: The answer is there, but the reason the question asked for is missing.
codes.description: Gives an answer, claim or 'show that' conclusion without the reasoning or working the question requires.
codes.example: 'Which ball lands first? They land at the same time.' with no reasoning about equal acceleration.

tell_apart.how: COM_WORK_NOT_SHOWN is for missing calculation steps; this code is for a missing explanation in words.
If an explanation is there but uses loose words, use COM_IMPRECISE_TERMS.

codes.remediation: Claim-evidence-reasoning frame.

codes.name: Work Not Shown
codes.student_help: Write the formula, then the numbers in it, then the answer.
codes.description: A calculation answer with no formula, substitution or steps where the question expects them, so the method cannot be checked or credited.
codes.example: Writes 'a = 2.4 m/s²' with no equation or substitution.

tell_apart.how: If the answer is wrong and there is no work, it is likely a guess: use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS. Use this code when the answer is right or close and only the steps are missing.
For a missing explanation in words, use COM_UNSUPPORTED_ANSWER.

codes.remediation: GRASS layout model: Given, Required, Analysis, Solution, Statement.

codes.name: Missing Labels / Definitions
codes.student_help: A graph, diagram or variable is missing labels, so it is unclear what it shows.
codes.description: Leaves out axis labels, scales, diagram labels or the 'let x be ...' definition that the work needs.
codes.example: Draws a free-body diagram with arrows but no force names.

tell_apart.how: COM_MISSING_UNITS is for a final numerical answer; this code is for diagrams, graphs and tables.

codes.remediation: Graph checklist card.

codes.name: Imprecise Terms
codes.plain_name: Used an everyday word where a subject term was needed
codes.student_help: Use the exact subject word instead of an everyday one.
codes.description: The idea is right but is stated with everyday or loose words where a specific scientific term is needed, so the answer is ambiguous.
codes.example: Writes 'the speed changes direction' or uses 'weight' for mass.

tell_apart.how: If no reasoning is given at all, use COM_UNSUPPORTED_ANSWER.
If the wrong word shows a wrong idea (the student really thinks sugar melts in water), use the matching concept (CON) code instead.

codes.remediation: Word wall with paired everyday and scientific terms.

codes.name: Observation vs Inference
codes.plain_name: Mixed up what you saw with what it means
codes.student_help: Observations are what you saw, heard or measured; put explanations in the analysis.
codes.description: In lab or data questions, reports an explanation as if it were observed, or lists observations where an analysis or conclusion is asked for. Includes conclusions that go beyond the data.
codes.example: Observation: 'friction slowed the cart' (what was measured was the distance).

tell_apart.how: STR_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN is about how the investigation is planned; this code is about how results are written up.

codes.remediation: Two-column observation / inference sort.

codes.name: Blank / Time Attrition
codes.student_help: This part was left blank.
codes.description: Leaves a question or part with no attempt, from time pressure or a frustration block.
codes.example: A whole question with no writing at all.

tell_apart.how: If any work was started, use TST_ABANDONED_WORK.
If other parts of the same question are answered, use TST_SKIPPED_PART.

codes.remediation: Prerequisite baseline probe on that topic.

codes.name: Skipped Part
codes.student_help: One part of the question was skipped while the others were answered.
codes.description: Answers some parts of a multi-part question and leaves another out, likely without noticing.
codes.example: Asked for the range and the maximum height; gives only the range.

tell_apart.how: If the whole question is empty, use TST_BLANK.
If the student answered something else instead of what was asked, use COM_ANSWERED_DIFFERENT_QUESTION.

codes.remediation: Part checklist habit.

codes.name: Distractor Trap
codes.plain_name: Middle step taken as the answer
codes.student_help: A middle step was treated as the final answer.
codes.description: Takes an intermediate value or a tempting wrong option as the final answer.
codes.example: Boxes the horizontal component of velocity as the final speed.

tell_apart.how: If the work just stops, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION; this code is for presenting the wrong value as final.
If there is no work behind the choice, use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS.

codes.remediation: 'Is this what was asked?' stop sign.

codes.name: Abandoned Work
codes.student_help: A good start was stopped or crossed out before reaching an answer.
codes.description: Starts a valid approach, then stops or crosses it out partway with no answer.
codes.example: Starts resolving forces on the incline, then crosses it out with no answer.

tell_apart.how: If nothing was written, use TST_BLANK.
If the work reaches a result one step short of the target, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION.

codes.remediation: First-step confidence warm-up, then the same problem.

codes.name: Unchecked Answer
codes.student_help: A quick check would show this answer cannot be right, like a negative length.
codes.description: Gives an answer a quick check would show is impossible or absurd, and does not notice.
codes.example: Reports a car's stopping distance as 4500 km.

tell_apart.how: Code the slip that caused the answer as well when it is visible; this code records that the impossible result was not caught.

codes.remediation: Estimate-then-check habit.

codes.name: Misread Given
codes.student_help: A number or sign in the question was read wrong.
codes.description: Misreads a number, sign or symbol printed in the question.
codes.example: Question says 45 cm; student uses 45 m.

tell_apart.how: If the slip happens between the student's own lines, use FAC_COPY_ERROR.
If the value is read right but used in the wrong place, use STR_WRONG_SUBSTITUTION.

codes.remediation: Given-data check habit.

codes.name: Unworked Guess
codes.student_help: An answer was written with no working, and it is not right.
codes.description: Writes a wrong final answer with no working shown, suggesting a guess.
codes.example: Writes 'Fnet = 50 N' with no work; the answer is 18 N.

tell_apart.how: If the answer is right but the work is missing, use COM_WORK_NOT_SHOWN.

codes.remediation: Show-one-step routine.

codes.name: Reference Sheet Not Used
codes.student_help: If a value or formula is on the data sheet or periodic table, look it up instead of remembering it.
codes.description: Gets a value, constant or formula wrong that was printed on the provided data sheet, formula sheet or periodic table.
codes.example: Uses G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹² when the data sheet gives 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹.

tell_apart.how: If the formula or value was NOT provided, use the matching recall (FAC) code.

codes.remediation: Reference-sheet scavenger hunt before the test.
